label: prop:alpha-em-categorical-trace-ratio
title: Algebraic identity: $\alpha_{EM} = h^2 / [q \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,9}) \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5})]$
html:
Let R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}] be the base ring. Let h = q - q^{-1} denote the skein parameter. Let T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} be the two genus-4-saturating torus knots ((T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}) is the unique pair of genus-4 torus knots). Let \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q denote the top-channel decoration of a torus knot (Top-channel decoration \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{m,p}) = q^{w} - q^{-w} of a torus knot). The bare electromagnetic fine-structure constant 1/\alpha_{EM} = q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q (Electromagnetic coupling from the antisymmetric braiding and force-carrier crossings) admits the categorical-trace-ratio decomposition:

  \boxed{\;\;
    \alpha_{EM}
    \;=\;
    \frac{h^{2}}{q \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,9}) \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5})}
  \;\;}

Derivation

By Top-channel decoration \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{m,p}) = q^{w} - q^{-w} of a torus knot, \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{m,p}) = q^{w} - q^{-w} with w = (m-1)p, the bar-odd part of the eigenvalue q^{w} by which the braid (\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_{m-1})^{p} acts in the trivial representation of H_m(q). Both knots here are presented on their braid index (2 \le 9 and 3 \le 5).

For T_{2,9}, w = 9, so \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,9}) = q^{9} - q^{-9} = h\,[9]_q. For 2-strand knots this agrees with the sum of the two Hecke characters, q^{9} + (-q^{-1})^{9}.

For T_{3,5}, w = 10, so \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5}) = q^{10} - q^{-10} = h\,[10]_q. Here the sum of the three characters on V_{(3)}, V_{(2,1)}, V_{(1,1,1)} would instead give q^{10} - 1 + q^{-10}, because \chi_{(2,1)}((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^{5}) = -1; the identity uses the top-channel value, not that sum.

Substitution produces the result:

  \frac{h^{2}}{q \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,9}) \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5})}
  \;=\;
  \frac{h^{2}}{q \cdot h\,[9]_q \cdot h\,[10]_q}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q}
  \;=\;
  \alpha_{EM}.

\square

Numerical verification

The algebraic identity holds over R at every invertible q with h = q - q^{-1} invertible. Evaluating both sides at the proton-pinned substrate parameter q_0 = 1.1099785828\ldots reproduces \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} = 1/(q_0\,[9]_{q_0}\,[10]_{q_0}) = 7.30870156 \times 10^{-3} (q_0\,[9]_{q_0}\,[10]_{q_0} = 136.823209), in exact agreement with Electromagnetic coupling from the antisymmetric braiding and force-carrier crossings. Table: Numerical verification of \alpha_{EM} trace-ratio lists the intermediate quantities at the primary proton anchor alongside the legacy muon anchor (q_0^{(\mu)} = 1.1099785956\ldots, where \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} = 7.30870098 \times 10^{-3}, a relative shift of 7.94 \times 10^{-8} between anchors while the two sides of the identity agree identically at each fixed anchor).

Expressing the relationship as a trace ratio on the q-dimension layer reformulates existing projection identities.
